hypotheses.reasoning: Message msg-595676 at catalog.updates partition 2, offset 145600, has a NUL byte at position 1860, so its JSON can't be parsed. index-worker nacks it and gets it redelivered over and over: attempt 14 by 19:45:46, and the log says no max-retries is configured. That blocks partition 2. Lag there climbs from about 1k messages (49s) to more than 13k (up to 774s) after 19:46. Because the worker is just retrying one message, CPU stays normal, which fits the alert. Other noise doesn't fit: status-poller errors come from a deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint, metrics-agent drops samples at its exporter, and a single GC pause comes before the failures without explaining them. I found no deploys.
A corrupt payload written by the producer (catalog-svc) could be called a data problem. But what stalls the queue is the consumer jamming on that one message.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-595676 (catalog.updates[2]@145600) to a dead-letter queue, or skip it by committing past that offset, so partition 2 starts draining again. Set a max-retries limit with dead-lettering on index-worker. Then check how catalog-svc produced a payload containing a NUL byte, and re-index that catalog item.
